item.title: Queen's Distance Track's Jude Wheeler-Dee sets history and runs fastest time in the nation
item.description: Queen's Distance Track had a successful weekend competing as the only non-NCAA Division One school competing at the Cornell Invitational. Queen's placed third in the seven school event, behind host Cornell and the University of Albany.

item.title: Queen's Women's Rugby Head Coach Dan Valley named Attack Coach for Canada's National U21 squad
item.description: Queen's Women's Rugby Head Coach Dan Valley was named the Attack Coach for Canada's National U21 squad by Rugby Canada.

item.title: Evie Carr named NCWP Rookie of the Year; five Gaels named NCWP All-Canadians
item.description: Queen's Water Polo had five student-athletes named All-Canadians by National Collegiate Water Polo for the 2025-26 season, as well as one major award winner, with Evie Carr being named the NCWP Rookie of the Year.

item.title: GAELS TRIUMPH OVER VARSITY BLUES IN FOUR SET WIN
item.description: The Queen's Gaels defeated the Toronto Varsity Blues in four sets on Friday night on the road. Coming into the game, both teams stood at an 11-5 record, hungry to earn another win and move up in the OUA standings. Leading the Gaels offense was Pascale Galarneau (Health Sciences) with 17 kills and 2 service aces, while Claire Carter (Business) and Abigail McAlpine (Arts & Science) each contributed 12 kills. item.title: 2026 season ticket packages for defending Yates Cup champion Queen’s Football on sale NOW
item.description: Queen's Football is defending the Yates Cup in 2026; make sure you're along for the ride!

item.title: Causeway Clash: Queen’s and RMC commemorate 140-years of rivalry, in 2026 Carr-Harris Cup
item.description: Queen's Men's Hockey and their crosstown rivals, the RMC Paladins, will clash on the ice for the second time this regular season on Saturday, Feb. 7. This time, however, the matchup moves beyond the historic confines of Memorial Centre and the close-quarters intensity of Constantine Arena to the bright lights of Slush Puppie Place downtown, and with a trophy in the building and citywide bragging rights on the line.

item.title: Gaels Dominate Nipissing 81-56 in Convincing Home Win
item.description: The Queen's Gaels women's basketball team defeated the Nipissing Lakers 81-56 in a convincing home game. The Gaels showcased sharp shooting, tough defence, and balanced scoring to take control of the game from start to finish.

item.title: Gaels Secure a Huge 111-69 Home Victory Against Nipissing
item.description: The Queen's Gaels men's basketball team dominated the Nipissing Lakers on Friday, February 6, securing a huge 111-69 home victory. The Gaels showcased sharp shooting, relentless defence, and a balanced offensive attack to control the game from start to finish.

item.title: Queen’s Drops 3–2 Overtime Decision to McGill.
item.description: Queen's Men's Hockey wrapped up its home schedule Friday night at the Memorial Centre, honouring graduating players, Lucas Peric (Economics), Nolan Hutcheson (Health Studies), Kolton Cousins (Arts & Sciences), Tanner Wickware (Graduate Studies), and Gaels captain Jack Duff (Biology) before puck drop against the McGill Redbirds. In front of a packed house, the Gaels put forth a strong effort but ultimately fell 3–2 in overtime in their final home game of the 2025–26 season.

item.title: GAELS FALL 3-0 TO VARSITY BLUES ON THE ROAD
item.description: The Queen's Gaels fell 3-0 to the Toronto Varsity Blues on Friday night on the road. This loss marks the end of a five-game winning streak for the Gaels, however, they will look to seek redemption tomorrow night. Leading the Queen's offense tonight was Nikola Mitrovic (Economics) and Reed Venning (Arts & Science) who each put up 9 kills and 1 service ace. Setter Chris Zimmerman (Arts) orchestrated the offense with 26 assists, as well as picking up a kill and a service ace.
